q-69925.name: Question 3
q-69925.worked_solution:
To compute

$$
\frac{3xz}{4}÷\frac{2z}{5},
$$

we just need to multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3xz}{4}÷\frac{2z}{5} & = \\ \frac{3xz}{4}\cdot \frac{5}{2z} & = \\ \frac{15xz}{8z} & = \\ \frac{15x\cancel{z}}{8\cancel{z}} & = \\ \frac{15x}{8} & \end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the final step, we canceled out a common factor of $z$ in the numerator and denominator.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-64}{x-5}÷\frac{(x-8)^{2}}{x-5} & = \\ \frac{{x}^{2}-64}{x-5}\cdot \frac{x-5}{(x-8)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{(x-8)(x+8)}{x-5}\cdot \frac{x-5}{(x-8)(x-8)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{(x-8)}(x+8)}{\cancel{x-5}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{x-5}}{\cancel{(x-8)}(x-8)} & = \\ (x+8)\cdot \frac{1}{(x-8)} & = \\ \frac{x+8}{x-8}\end{aligned}
